saw_lines: Foraging buyers commit slowly. They try a free mini course first, then decide whether a paid course is worth the money.
So the sale turns on line one, where a new buyer decides to act, and your ads give them no reason to.
Your site offers subscribe and save, yet 0 of 19 ads mention it. Put the offer in the first line of three new ads and on the creative.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 1 Nov 2026
points: Your site offers subscribe and save, yet 0 of 19 ads mention it. A new buyer comparing courses has no reason to commit today. Put the offer in the first line of three new ads and on the creative.

None of your 30 ads mentions a subscription, so the saving that brings a buyer back never reaches anyone. Run two ads for past buyers with subscribe and save as the headline, aimed at people who already bought a course.
The same course copy runs in 7 of 19 ads, so a buyer who sees one ad sees the same pitch again. Keep the copy, but change the opening line and the creative in each, so every version reads as new.

None of your 30 ads shows a proof number, so a buyer weighing a paid course has nothing concrete to trust. Collect one real figure, such as a review count, then open two new ads with it on the creative.

ads_1: Fresh opening lines with subscribe and save, tested against the current course copy
soc_1: Brand social strategy across Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube
